subject.title: Feature: diagnostics stuck-session recovery ladder (steer → nudge → abort)

question: Should OpenClaw diagnostics actively steer and nudge sessions in core before aborting them, and what liveness, eligibility, and channel-delivery contract must gate those actions?
rationale: This is a new automated recovery policy and configuration surface. The correct default, escalation timing, and whether diagnostic recovery may generate session-visible messages cannot be resolved safely from code alone.

options.title: Approve a guarded core ladder
options.body: Define a small core policy with mandatory Gateway-liveness and diagnosis gates, persisted/idempotent escalation state, and abort retained as the final fallback.

options.title: Keep diagnostics observational
options.body: Retain warning, diagnosis, and explicit operator actions while leaving automated recovery orchestration to deployments or plugins.

options.title: Defer until diagnosis lands
options.body: Treat read-only diagnosis as the prerequisite and revisit active recovery after operators can reliably distinguish active, stale, and unsafe-to-act-on sessions.

recommendation.title: Approve a guarded core ladder
recommendation.body: Define a small core policy with mandatory Gateway-liveness and diagnosis gates, persisted/idempotent escalation state, and abort retained as the final fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work appears connected to diagnostics recovery scheduling, making this the strongest available routing signal for the policy boundary.
